sentences.text: The holotype fossil consists of a nearly complete but partially articulated right wing.
The estimated length of the humerus is about nine centimeters.
This bone features a large deltopectoral crest whose expansion exceeds the shaft width.
The ulna possesses a single, clearly distinct oval depression on its upper articulation surface.
This wing is estimated to be 111% the length of the largest known Archaeopteryx specimen.
The fossil slab showing a right wing was discovered in November 2017.
The fossil was discovered by amateur paleontologist Roland Pöschl at the Alte Schöpfel quarry near Mörnsheim in Bavaria.
The species Alcmonavis poeschli was named and described in 2019 by Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut, Helmut Tischlinger, and Christian Foth.
Alcmonavis lived in the area of present-day Germany during the Late Jurassic period.
Alcmonavis lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
Some researchers still argue that the original fossil was a specimen of Archaeopteryx rather than a new species.
In early 2026, O'Connor and Marugán-Lobón argued that Alcmonavis and Ostromia are junior synonyms of Archaeopteryx.
